summary: The note explains that the Clean Water Act's formal name is the Federal Water Pollution Control Act. The original version was enacted in 1948 and was rewritten in its modern form in 1972 through the Federal Water Pollution Control Act Amendments of 1972. Later amendments, including the Clean Water Act of 1977 and the Water Quality Act of 1987, introduced major changes.
one_line: The Clean Water Act's formal name is the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, with its modern form dating to 1972 and later amendments in 1977 and 1987.
key_facts: The formal name of the Clean Water Act is the Federal Water Pollution Control Act.
The first Federal Water Pollution Control Act (FWPCA) was enacted in 1948.
The FWPCA took on its modern form when completely rewritten in 1972.
The 1972 rewrite was an act entitled the Federal Water Pollution Control Act Amendments of 1972.
Major changes to the law were subsequently introduced via amendatory legislation.
The Clean Water Act of 1977 was amendatory legislation that introduced major changes to the FWPCA.
The Water Quality Act of 1987 was amendatory legislation that introduced major changes to the FWPCA.
